methods.evidence: Precedent is direct: Betfair's Opta POTM market 'is settled from Opta's own website and rankings, and not related to who is selected via broadcasters, pundits or sponsors' — award markets increasingly settle on algorithmic ratings. Sofascore and WhoScored both publish that their ratings are deterministic event-driven algorithms (Sofascore: 5 action categories, baseline 6.5; WhoScored: 200+ stats, baseline 6.0, live-updated). Danish media/fantasy products typically license one of these feeds. SPECULATIVE: whether Holdet specifically mirrors one is unverified — that is exactly what this cheap experiment determines from data already cached.
methods.apply: A one-off offline audit script over cached stats_rN.json (513 winners already decoded) plus scraped historical ratings for the same fixtures. Outcome branches: (a) deterministic match found -> method 4's rating weights are fit to reproduce that provider's rating directly (regression on events, no award data needed) and MOTM becomes argmax-of-simulated-rating with near-zero label noise; (b) no match -> stay with methods 3/4 trained on 513 history. Either way it fixes the target definition before weeks of model fitting — highest information-per-effort item in this list.

methods.name: Correlated residual-BPS via copula/conditional-mean coupling to simulated events (fixes hauler underprojection)
methods.what: Do not draw residual (non-event) BPS independently of the player's simulated events. On big attacking days a player's pass/dribble/foul-drawn volume BPS is also elevated (more touches in dangerous areas, game flows through them), and team winning inflates everyone's volume stats on that side. Couple the residual-BPS draw to (a) the player's own simulated goal+assist count and (b) team result, via a Gaussian copula or a simple estimated conditional-mean shift. Without this, the bonus model systematically under-ranks haulers in exactly the sims where captaincy pays — reproducing the engine's audited under-projection of premium players in a new stream.
methods.evidence: PARTLY SPECULATIVE (mechanism is estimable, no published effect size): jphelps13's open BPS analysis shows the BPS->bonus relationship is strongly position-dependent with highest variance for forwards, and season-level fits underfit badly (residual deviance 2015 on 966 df) precisely because per-match dependence structure is lost — evidence that independence assumptions break. OpenFPL's benchmark shows hauler-category RMSE is where models separate. The correlation itself is directly measurable from vaastav per-match data: regress per-match (bps - event_bps) on same-match goals/assists/result before choosing copula strength.
methods.apply: Modifies method 1's residual draw: residual_i = base_i + beta_pos * (sim goals_i + assists_i) + gamma * win_i + eps_i, with beta/gamma fit offline from historical per-match BPS decompositions. Zero architectural change — one extra line in the per-sim BPS computation. Validate by comparing simulated vs historical joint distribution of (returns, bonus): the diagnostic is P(bonus=3 | goal scored) by position.

methods.name: Bookmaker MOTM/POTM props as a calibration anchor — with documented goalscorer-bias correction and power de-vig
methods.what: Where a book quotes MOTM/POTM (Betfair Opta POTM on PL; Sky Bet and others quote MOTM on big matches/tournaments), de-vig and use as an external anchor for the MOTM model — consistent with the engine's odds-first design. Two twists the literature demands: (1) MOTM fields are 22+ runner longshot markets, where proportional de-vig is known-bad — use power/Shin de-vig for the field; (2) documented recreational bias: books shade star strikers short 'regardless of whether their overall game warrants favourite status', so calibrate the model to beat, not match, the prop on defenders/GKs.
methods.evidence: Betfair launched an algorithmically-settled Opta POTM market (April 2023) — machine-settleable, hence quoted more widely than pundit-voted MOTM. Betting guides note 'MOTM pricing varies significantly between books because it is a relatively new market without the competitive efficiency of match results' and that pricing is 'heavily biased toward likely goalscorers' — i.e. it is an anchor with exploitable slack, unlike 1X2. FPL Review's public research shows a fitted goalscoring model can be MORE predictive than bookmaker-odds implications, supporting calibrate-then-deviate rather than pure anchoring. SPECULATIVE: WC2026 MOTM prop coverage by the engine's single free book is unverified.
methods.apply: Extends the odds-ingestion stage with an optional motm_props.json per match; a small calibration step (offline) fits a logistic map from model MOTM probability to de-vigged prop probability, reporting bias by position. Where props exist they become a validation baseline in the harness ('MOTM hit-rate vs props') and a soft prior; where absent, the model runs standalone. Also add power de-vig as an option for ALL many-runner player props (anytime scorer included) — proportional de-vig on longshot fields is a known weakness already flagged in the engine.

methods.name: Hierarchical Bayesian player-rating priors with explicit missing-data handling (Egidi & Gabry) for sparse tournament data
methods.what: Fit each player's latent 'award propensity' (intercept in methods 3/4) as a hierarchical Bayesian model over historical match ratings — partial pooling across position, team and league — with explicit modeling of missing observations (DNPs, players from low-coverage leagues). Critical at a World Cup where most players have 3-7 observed matches and Holdet 513 history gives at most a handful of winners: unpooled MLE intercepts would be garbage, and ignoring missingness biases toward players who only play when in form.
methods.evidence: Egidi & Gabry (JQAS 2018) built exactly this for Italian fantacalcio newspaper ratings — the closest published analogue to Holdet MOTM settlement — comparing hierarchical models on hold-out predictive accuracy and finding that modeling the missing-observation mechanism materially matters; they validated with posterior predictive checks on out-of-sample second-half-of-season ratings. Follow-up Bayesian performance-prediction case studies (Frontiers 2025) extend the approach. Their headline: even 'a few variables from a freely available dataset' supports useful player-level rating prediction when pooling is done right.
methods.apply: Offline fit (can be simple empirical-Bayes / ridge shrinkage to stay stdlib: player intercept = league-position mean + shrunken residual weighted by matches observed) producing a per-player prior table cached as JSON; consumed as the intercept term by the MOTM logit/rating models. Also reusable by the existing research-overlay blend as a principled replacement for hand-set w on 'form' multipliers.

methods.name: Sub-time hazard minutes model as the award-eligibility gate (upgrade from 'starters = 60+')
methods.what: Awards sharpen the cost of the crude minutes model: bonus and MOTM go overwhelmingly to players on the pitch 60+ minutes (BPS itself pays 6/3 for >60/1-60, and rating baselines accrue with time), so 'starters treated as 60+' overstates award odds for early-hook attackers and understates super-sub scenarios. Replace with a discrete sub-time distribution per player (e.g., P(off at 60-75), P(off 75-90), P(full 90), P(sub on at t)) drawn per sim, conditioned on game state (winning teams sub attackers earlier) and player role, fit from cached minutes history (Holdet 224/562/342 events already decode starts/DNP).
methods.evidence: OpenFPL's benchmark localizes the commercial edge in exactly this input: FPL Review beats OpenFPL only on zeros/blanks 'likely due to proprietary expected-minutes data', while OpenFPL wins on haulers — i.e. minutes modeling is the single input where paid services still dominate open models. FPL Optimized publicly flags 'players either play 90 or 0' as its main sim limitation. The engine's own realized-minutes priors work (core/realized.py, per user memory) already fixed a price-prior bias — this extends the same data to within-match timing. Effect size on awards specifically: SPECULATIVE, but BPS minute-band points alone are 3 vs 6 and every count stat in methods 1-2 scales with minutes.
methods.apply: Upgrades the minutes stage of the per-player event simulation: draw a sub-off/sub-on time per player per sim from a small categorical hazard table (fit offline from cached started/benched/DNP feeds plus realized minutes), then scale all count rates and BPS/DC/MOTM eligibility by simulated minutes. This is a shared prerequisite that method 1/2/3/4 all consume, and it directly attacks the engine's listed 'CRUDE minutes' weakness with the same cached data.

methods.name: Category-stratified award validation in the backtesting harness: MOTM hit-rate vs props/ratings baselines, bonus as a separate event stream
methods.what: Adopt OpenFPL's stratified evaluation design for the new award streams: score bonus and MOTM separately from base points, stratified by return category (zeros/blanks/tickers/haulers) and position, with three baselines per stream — (a) naive (bonus: historical per-player bonus/90; MOTM: highest-priced/goal-favorite player), (b) de-vigged bookmaker prop where quoted, (c) top-rated-player-by-provider. Report MOTM top-1 hit-rate and top-3 (for FPL bonus, exact 3/2/1 allocation accuracy), plus calibration curves of predicted vs realized award probability.
methods.evidence: OpenFPL demonstrates that aggregate RMSE hides where models differ — its stratified tables show the open model beating a commercial service on haulers while losing on zeros, invisible in pooled metrics; award points are maximally concentrated in the hauler stratum so pooled validation would mask exactly the improvement being bought. FPL Review's own 'Ultimate Truth' article benchmarks models against a 'perfect model' upper bound — the same idea gives an award-stream noise ceiling (MOTM is 1-of-22; even the perfect model has bounded hit-rate, estimable from the entropy of the fitted logit).
methods.apply: Drops into the category-stratified harness now being built: awards register as independent event streams keyed to the same cached settlement feeds (Holdet 513 for MOTM; FPL API bonus/bps fields for the port). Round-over-round, log hit-rates vs the three baselines; promotion rule: ship the MOTM model to production xPts only when it beats the goal-favorite baseline out of sample for two consecutive rounds.
